mortensor: notes for Claude Code sessions

Source: CLAUDE.md

Read first: dev/progress.md (status per work package), the work package row in dev/implementation-plan.md, and dev/revamp-plan.md for the design.

Layout

Path Content
R/data-*.R Axes, mt_data container, regrouping, validation, exposures, adapters (HMD, ONS, GENESIS), simulated examples, ons_data documentation
data/, data-raw/ ons_data, ons_cause_groups (data-raw/ons_data.R); de_deaths, de_population, de_cause_groups (data-raw/de_data.R)
R/harmonise-*.R PCLM engine and mt_ungroup(), smoothing and preprocessing steps
R/model-*.R Model specifications, fitting, forecast draws
R/hierarchy.R Hierarchies of strata, aggregation, reconciliation
R/eval-*.R Backtests and scoring
R/derive-*.R Life tables and derived quantities
dev/ Plans, review, progress log, calibration study, package comparison script (not built into the package)

Conventions

  • R >= 4.3.0. Imports: data.table, Matrix, methods, parallel, splines, stats, utils. Everything else is in Suggests and guarded with need_pkg() or requireNamespace(); tests use skip_if_not_installed().
  • Exported verbs carry the mt_ prefix; model constructors are nouns (lee_carter(), rwd(), tucker3(), apc_bayes()). A test checks that exports do not clash with base, stats, utils, data.table, dplyr, forecast, generics, demography or StMoMo.
  • Errors and warnings: mt_abort(msg, class = "<topic>") and mt_warn(msg, class = "<topic>") give classes mt_error_<topic> and mt_warning_<topic>; tests check classes, not messages. Messages only via mt_inform() (silent unless options(mortensor.verbose = TRUE)).
  • data.table inside the package: column names used in non-standard evaluation go into utils::globalVariables() in R/mortensor-package.R. Never name a local variable like a column used in the same [ call.
  • Plot snapshots (vdiffr) are made with ggplot2 >= 4.0; regenerate them after an intended change or a ggplot2 release (testthat::snapshot_review()).
  • Precomputed vignette results: vignettes/comparison-results.rds comes from dev/compare-packages.R (about one hour); the bamp vignette from dev/precompute-vignettes.R.
  • Randomness: functions that simulate take seed = NULL and use with_seed(); parallel code uses parallel with L’Ecuyer streams.
  • Code adapted from other packages carries a header with source, version, licence and authors.
  • No print()/cat() for messages outside print methods; plots return ggplot objects; no files written outside tempdir().

Commands

Rscript -e 'roxygen2::roxygenise()'                 # docs and NAMESPACE
Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'                       # unit tests
R CMD INSTALL . && Rscript -e 'lintr::lint_package()'   # lint
R CMD build . && R CMD check --as-cran mortensor_*.tar.gz

Workflow

  • CI budget: pushes to development branches start no workflows. Run the unit tests and lint locally before each commit. Pull requests (when ready for review) and pushes to main run the Ubuntu checks; Windows and R-devel run monthly; macOS only by hand (workflow_dispatch with platforms = all).

  • One work package per commit or pull request; update dev/progress.md and NEWS.md in the same change.

  • Documentation is part of every feature. After a feature works (tests, lint), review and update in the same change: roxygen docs (roxygenise()), README, NEWS, the vignettes that use or should use it (re-knit precomputed ones with dev/precompute-vignettes.R), the function map (vignettes/articles/function-map.Rmd), the FAQ, and _pkgdown.yml (reference index and articles). Then build the pkgdown site locally (pkgdown::build_site(), offline: options(pkgdown.internet = FALSE)) and check that every exported function is indexed and every page renders. The site is deployed from main by .github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml.

  • The package is public and labelled as experimental, vibe-coded software (README notice and lifecycle badge, DESCRIPTION, package help, startup message). Keep these notices.

  • Correctness first: run the unit tests; new methods get tests that check them against the published method or a reference implementation (published numbers, the authors’ code, an established package), and exact identities where they hold. Forecast performance (coverage, CRPS, accuracy) depends on the data and is checked by the user with backtests; the repository has no performance benchmarks with thresholds.

  • Data from other packages (HMD extracts in StMoMo and demography) is loaded in tests and vignettes, never copied into the repository. The owner’s German data stays outside the repository. Exceptions, with the owner’s agreement: ons_data (ONS, Open Government Licence) and the German regional data de_deaths/de_population (Destatis, Datenlizenz Deutschland by-2-0), built by the scripts in data-raw/.
